scope.description: Hand-researched deepening pass for English Legendary Collection and five rows that show reprint memory, fireworks Reverse Holofoil, theme-deck exceptions, and late-Wizards nostalgia assembly.

sources.title: Local English WoC release catalog: Legendary Collection
Pokemon TCG API v2 set record: Legendary Collection
Bulbapedia: Legendary Collection (TCG)
Bulbapedia: Holofoil / Reverse Holofoil

claims.text: The local catalog and Pokemon TCG API model Legendary Collection with a May 24, 2002 English release date; Bulbapedia also lists May 24, 2002.
The local catalog, Pokemon TCG API, and Bulbapedia model Legendary Collection as a 110-card set.
Bulbapedia describes Legendary Collection as composed of reprints from Base Set, Jungle, Fossil, and Team Rocket, with no main Japanese equivalent.

Bulbapedia says Legendary Collection introduced Reverse Holofoil prints with Holofoil throughout the card except the artwork window, and says this expansion's Reverse Holofoil has a fireworks-like pattern.
Bulbapedia lists Lava and Turmoil as the Legendary Collection theme decks and notes exclusive non-holo prints of Charizard, Dark Blastoise, and Dark Raichu tied to those decks.
The local catalog's attention rows include Charizard, Dark Blastoise, Dark Raichu, Gyarados, Venusaur, Zapdos, and other reprinted Kanto-era icons.

The local catalog's credited-artist clusters for Legendary Collection are led by Ken Sugimori, Mitsuhiro Arita, Kagemaru Himeno, and Keiji Kinebuchi, with single-row credits including Christopher Rush, Shin-ichi Yoshida, Sumiyoshi Kizuki, and Miki Tanaka.

Legendary Collection matters because it turns early Pokemon memory into a new object: familiar Base/Jungle/Fossil/Team Rocket cards return under a new set mark, fireworks Reverse Holofoil treatment, theme-deck exceptions, and collector nostalgia as the organizing principle.

not_claiming: same artwork means same set or same foil treatment
steps: Confirm Legendary Collection set id base6 and the printed number before comparing to Base Set, Jungle, Fossil, or Team Rocket originals.
Record whether a listing claims regular holo, non-holo theme-deck exclusive, or fireworks Reverse Holofoil treatment.
Do not collapse Legendary Collection reprints into their original-set rows for pricing, evidence, or wants.
If a listing says 'reverse' or shows fireworks foil, ask for clear images of the whole card surface, number, and set symbol before routing.
special_identification_instructions.summary: Legendary Collection identity is reprint-plus-treatment: source lineage, set mark, foil state, and theme-deck exceptions all matter.
special_identification_instructions.trigger: Identifying or comparing Legendary Collection cards, especially reverse holos or theme-deck non-holos.

narrative.why_it_matters: Legendary Collection is not a normal expansion so much as a memory machine. Wizards takes the early binder canon, gives it a new set mark, and then covers the card body in fireworks foil. The result is wonderfully strange: the same childhood images, but louder, shinier, and suddenly separate from their origin rows.

sources.title: Local English WoC card row: Legendary Collection Charizard
Pokemon TCG API v2 card record: Legendary Collection Charizard
Bulbapedia: Charizard (Base Set 4)
Bulbapedia: Legendary Collection (TCG)

claims.text: The local catalog and Pokemon TCG API identify Charizard as Legendary Collection number 3, a Rare Holo Stage 2 Fire row credited to Mitsuhiro Arita.

Bulbapedia's Charizard page lists a Legendary Collection print of the Base Set Charizard card, while the Legendary Collection page lists a non-holo Charizard as a Lava Theme Deck exclusive additional card.
The Pokemon TCG API records Charizard's Energy Burn Pokemon Power and Fire Spin attack for this Legendary Collection row.

Legendary Collection Charizard matters because it is not simply Base Charizard again; it is Base Charizard reframed by fireworks reverse holo possibility, a new set mark, and a Lava deck non-holo branch.

not_claiming: Base Set and Legendary Collection Charizard are interchangeable
steps: Confirm Legendary Collection number 3/110 and set symbol before comparing to Base Set, Base Set 2, Stormfront, or later Charizard rows.
Record whether the listing claims regular holo, fireworks Reverse Holofoil, or Lava Theme Deck non-holo context.
Keep Energy Burn / Fire Spin as row text context, not physical proof.
If a seller image resembles Base Charizard, ask for set symbol, number, and foil-surface evidence.
special_identification_instructions.summary: Legendary Collection Charizard is a reprint identity with foil-state and Lava-deck branches; do not collapse it into Base Charizard.
special_identification_instructions.trigger: A listing or want references Legendary Collection Charizard, reverse holo Charizard, or Lava Theme Deck Charizard.

narrative.why_it_matters: Legendary Collection Charizard is memory with a flashbulb. The Arita image is already loaded with childhood gravity, but this set makes the collector ask a new question: which surface, which symbol, which treatment? The same dragon becomes a different artifact because the assembly changed around it.

sources.title: Local English WoC card row: Legendary Collection Dark Blastoise
Pokemon TCG API v2 card record: Legendary Collection Dark Blastoise
Bulbapedia: Dark Blastoise (Team Rocket 3)
Bulbapedia: Legendary Collection (TCG)

claims.text: The local catalog and Pokemon TCG API identify Dark Blastoise as Legendary Collection number 4, a Rare Holo Stage 2 Water row credited to Mitsuhiro Arita.

Bulbapedia says Dark Blastoise was first released in Team Rocket, later reprinted in Japanese Pokemon Web, later reprinted in Legendary Collection, and also reprinted as a Non Holofoil card in the Turmoil Theme Deck.
Bulbapedia's Legendary Collection page also lists Dark Blastoise as a Non Holo Turmoil Theme Deck exclusive additional card.

Legendary Collection Dark Blastoise matters because a Team Rocket identity returns inside a nostalgia set, with Pokemon Web, Legendary Collection holo, reverse holo, and Turmoil non-holo branches all nearby.

not_claiming: Team Rocket and Legendary Collection prints are interchangeable
steps: Separate Team Rocket, Pokemon Web, Legendary Collection holo/reverse, and Turmoil Theme Deck non-holo contexts before comparison.
Confirm Legendary Collection number 4/110 and set symbol for the English base6 row.
Record whether the listing claims regular holo, fireworks Reverse Holofoil, or Turmoil non-holo.
Ask for set symbol, number, and foil-surface photos if a listing only says Dark Blastoise.
special_identification_instructions.summary: Dark Blastoise crosses Team Rocket, Pokemon Web, Legendary Collection, and Turmoil branches; set and foil state must be explicit.
special_identification_instructions.trigger: A listing or want references Dark Blastoise, Legendary Collection, Pokemon Web, Team Rocket, or Turmoil Theme Deck.

narrative.human_title: Rocket water in the nostalgia machine
narrative.why_it_matters: Dark Blastoise is one of the rows where Legendary Collection shows its real trick. It is not just pulling from Base memory; it is pulling Team Rocket's darker vocabulary into a commemorative surface. The result is a card that feels familiar, villainous, and administratively fussy in exactly the way collectors end up caring about.

sources.title: Local English WoC card row: Legendary Collection Dark Raichu
Pokemon TCG API v2 card record: Legendary Collection Dark Raichu
Bulbapedia: Dark Raichu (Team Rocket 83)
Bulbapedia: Legendary Collection (TCG)

claims.text: The local catalog and Pokemon TCG API identify Dark Raichu as Legendary Collection number 7, a Rare Holo Stage 1 Lightning row credited to Mitsuhiro Arita.

Bulbapedia says Dark Raichu was included as a Secret card in Team Rocket, made especially for the English set by Wizards of the Coast, later printed in Japanese Crossing the Ruins..., and reprinted in Legendary Collection.

Bulbapedia notes the original Team Rocket Dark Raichu top-right text error and says it was corrected in the Legendary Collection reprint; it also says a Non Holofoil print was included in the Turmoil Theme Deck.
Bulbapedia's Legendary Collection page lists Dark Raichu as a Non Holo Turmoil Theme Deck exclusive additional card.
Legendary Collection Dark Raichu matters because it reprints one of Wizards' own English-origin secrets while visibly correcting text and adding fireworks and theme-deck branches.

steps: Separate Team Rocket 83/82, Japanese Crossing the Ruins, Legendary Collection 7/110, and Turmoil Theme Deck non-holo contexts.
Record whether the top-right evolution text is the original erroneous text or the Legendary Collection corrected text.
Record whether the listing claims regular holo, fireworks Reverse Holofoil, or Turmoil non-holo.
Treat corrected text as row-context evidence, not standalone physical authentication.
special_identification_instructions.summary: Dark Raichu has an English-origin secret-card lineage and a corrected-text Legendary Collection boundary.
special_identification_instructions.trigger: A listing or want references Dark Raichu, Team Rocket 83/82, Legendary Collection 7/110, corrected text, or Turmoil Theme Deck.

narrative.human_title: The secret card comes back corrected
narrative.why_it_matters: Dark Raichu is the most self-aware card in this pass. It began as an English-made secret, crossed into Japanese print history, then came back in Legendary Collection with corrected text and new foil possibilities. It is a small card-history knot, and exactly the sort of thing an agent should never flatten.

sources.title: Local English WoC card row: Legendary Collection Gyarados
Pokemon TCG API v2 card record: Legendary Collection Gyarados
Bulbapedia: Gyarados (Base Set 6)

claims.text: The local catalog and Pokemon TCG API identify Gyarados as Legendary Collection number 12, a Rare Holo Stage 1 Water row credited to Mitsuhiro Arita.
Bulbapedia says the Base Set Gyarados print was reprinted in Base Set 2 and Legendary Collection, and also notes a separate rare Japanese Pokemon Snap Best Photo Contest print by Ryouichi Abe.
The Pokemon TCG API records Gyarados's Dragon Rage and Bubblebeam attacks for the Legendary Collection row.

Legendary Collection Gyarados matters because it shows how ordinary-looking reprint rows can hide sharp lineage traps: Base Set, Base Set 2, Legendary Collection, and the separate Pokemon Snap photo contest branch all need different treatment.

not_claiming: photo contest branch is equivalent to Legendary Collection
steps: Confirm Legendary Collection number 12/110 and set symbol before comparing to Base Set or Base Set 2 Gyarados.
Do not route the Japanese Pokemon Snap Best Photo Contest print as the same row; it has different artwork and provenance.
Record whether the listing claims regular holo or fireworks Reverse Holofoil.
Ask for set symbol, number, and artwork evidence if a seller only says vintage Gyarados.
special_identification_instructions.summary: Legendary Collection Gyarados is a reprint row, but the Pokemon Snap photo branch is a separate high-risk lineage.
special_identification_instructions.trigger: A listing or want references Legendary Collection Gyarados, Base Set Gyarados, or Pokemon Snap Gyarados.

narrative.human_title: The familiar sea monster with a hidden photo ghost
narrative.why_it_matters: Gyarados looks straightforward until you follow the branches. Arita's Base-era monster returns in Legendary Collection, but nearby in the species history is the strange Ryouichi Abe Pokemon Snap contest print. That is why this catalog exists: the card is familiar, but the assembly is not simple.

sources.title: Local English WoC card row: Legendary Collection Mewtwo
Pokemon TCG API v2 card record: Legendary Collection Mewtwo
Bulbapedia: Mewtwo (Wizards Promo 3)

claims.text: The local catalog and Pokemon TCG API identify Mewtwo as Legendary Collection number 29, a Rare Basic Psychic row credited to Christopher Rush.
The local catalog and Pokemon TCG API credit this Legendary Collection Mewtwo row to Christopher Rush, making it a visual outlier among the set's mostly Japanese TCG artist clusters.

Bulbapedia's Wizards Promo Mewtwo page documents multiple Mewtwo promo branches tied to Mewtwo Strikes Back, Black Star Promos, and Japanese unnumbered promotional cards; those branches are not the same row as Legendary Collection Mewtwo.

Legendary Collection Mewtwo matters because it shows that not every nostalgia row is the obvious Base holo: a Christopher Rush rare sits beside Arita and Sugimori memory, reminding the agent to inspect artist and row identity instead of species fame alone.

not_claiming: all vintage Mewtwo rows share artist or promo lineage
steps: Confirm Legendary Collection number 29/110 and Christopher Rush credit before comparing to Base, promo, movie-stamp, or other Mewtwo rows.
Do not import Mewtwo Strikes Back stamp or Black Star promo assumptions into this row unless the listing explicitly shows that print.
Record whether the listing claims regular or fireworks Reverse Holofoil treatment.
Ask for set symbol, number, artist line, and full-card photos if a listing only says vintage Mewtwo.
special_identification_instructions.summary: Legendary Collection Mewtwo is a Christopher Rush rare, not the Base holo or movie-promo branch; artist line matters.
special_identification_instructions.trigger: A listing or want references Legendary Collection Mewtwo, vintage Mewtwo, Christopher Rush, or Mewtwo movie promo.

narrative.human_title: The odd artist credit in the memory set
narrative.why_it_matters: Mewtwo 29 is the quiet corrective to lazy nostalgia. Legendary Collection is full of huge familiar images, but this row asks the agent to notice Christopher Rush, a different branch of Mewtwo memory, and a non-holo rare slot. Species fame is not enough. The card has to be placed.
